observations: White HP printer with a flatbed scanner on top, placed on a blue floral bedsheet.
Photo 0 shows the front and top of the printer with the HP logo and a label on the right side.
Photo 1 shows the top and front control panel with buttons and a small LCD screen.
Photo 2 shows the rear view with the paper output tray open, revealing the internal paper path and a small white box (possibly a power adapter or ink cartridge holder) in front.
The label on photo 0 is partially legible and appears to say 'HP DeskJet 2710 series'.
The printer has visible signs of use: minor scuffs, dust, and smudges on the surface.
No visible damage or missing parts in the photos.
The control panel buttons are intact and the screen is dark (no power shown).

claims.claim: Fairly used - in good working condition
claims.evidence: Photos show physical condition but no proof of functionality. No power or operation shown.
Label on photo 0 reads 'HP DeskJet 2710 series'.

risks.risk: Printer may not be functional (e.g., no power, no print, no scan, no wireless connectivity)
risks.proof: Video or photo showing the printer powered on, printing a test page, scanning a document, and connecting to a wireless network.

risks.risk: Ink cartridges may be empty or missing
risks.proof: Photo showing the open cartridge compartment with cartridges installed and visible ink levels.

risks.risk: Internal components may be damaged or clogged (e.g., print head, paper feed mechanism)
risks.proof: Photo or video showing paper feeding smoothly and printing a clean test page.

proof_requests: Video or photo of the printer powered on and printing a test page.
Photo of the ink cartridge compartment with cartridges installed.
Photo or video showing the printer scanning a document.
Photo showing the printer connected to a wireless network (e.g., screen displaying network name).
response.reason: The model is identified from the label in photo 0, but the seller's claim of 'good working condition' cannot be verified from the photos alone. Functionality, ink status, and internal condition are hidden risks that must be proven before pricing.
